correctness.rationale: A strictly upper-triangular binary matrix B with Boolean B²=0 has disjoint sets S of nonzero rows and T of nonzero columns (any overlap would create a 2-step path). Off isolates, each index is S or T, and each active edge runs forward S to T. An ordered word with a=|S|, b=|T| encodes exactly one Ferrers inversion diagram lambda inside a×b, with ab−|lambda| permitted edges. For fixed j and lambda, the probability of any active zero row or column among 2^(ab−|lambda|) assignments is bounded by a*2^(−(b−|lambda|))+b*2^(−(a−|lambda|)), tending to zero. The exact isolated-vertex deletion convolution H_n=∑_u binom(n,u) H_(n-u)^0, Gaussian-binomial/partition-product majorant Q^(−2) and lower bound 2^floor(n²/4) imply isolates negligible. Pointwise counts normalized by 2^m² (even) tend to 2^(−j²−|lambda|), and by 2^(m(m+1)) (odd) to 2^(j−j²−|lambda|). Countable dominated convergence and Scheffe yield total variation, product law P_even(j,lambda)=(2^(−j²)/Z0)*Q*2^(−|lambda|), P_odd=(2^(j−j²)/Z1)*Q*2^(−|lambda|). Exhaustive direct n=1..6 integer counts 1,2,6,26,158,1330 corroborate combinatorial premises, not the n→∞ convergence.
